items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: I had George Gayno on, uh, who was a wonderful talker. I used to transcribe his lessons.

ctx.x: And this is on the New Orleans Ensemble Stock.

Yeah, it must be, uh, these, uh, I had George Gayno on, uh, who was a wonderful talker. I used to transcribe his lessons. About a dozen of his lessons, probably, on banjo. Then I got started, uh, back in the fifties, recording Mineta. He would teach all instruments. And, uh, still I have a chapter. I had Irvin Helfer, a young pianist from Chicago, recorded a lesson or two of his on piano. I would have a chapter by Mineta on the piano in the band, I guess, as they called it. That was another Otis Ferguson article…

items.title: George Guesnon Interview, 1965-09
items.q: That Bill Russell liked it so well. Him and his niece made a copy for me on a violin.

ctx.x: I bet it was. That was in the 20s. Oh, yeah, that's what it is.

But it's 30, yeah. Wow. He the prettiest of all the numbers I've ever written. I wrote it for my daughter when she died. I wrote it in Spanish. When she died? She died. She pulled me down. That Bill Russell liked it so well. Him and his niece made a copy for me on a violin. Yeah. Two violins together. Yeah. Yeah.
